mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp drop in WORKPLACES mobility will reduce weekday discretionary shopping trips after a short lag, so RETAIL_REC should fall relative to the last four weeks over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below its recent weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply depressed, households shift spending to nearby or online substitutes and make fewer retail visits, lowering RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after TRANSIT remains below -40 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +5.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS usage reflects warmer-weather leisure activity and broader outdoor circulation, which spills into more retail and recreation visits over the following month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points from its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days after PARKS posts a one-week increase of 10 points or more.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT recovers while WORKPLACES remain weak, retail mobility improves only modestly because commuting recovers faster than office attendance and does not yet sustain shopping demand.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES stay below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after TRANSIT improves while WORKPLACES remain below -15.

mechanism_narrative: A further decline in GROCERY_PHARM signals substitution toward fewer out-of-home errands overall; that same shopping compression should also reduce discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains below zero or weakens further.

mechanism_narrative: A weekly jump in PARKS paired with stable or improving TRANSIT indicates weather-driven outdoor movement rather than restriction-driven avoidance, and this combination should lift retail foot traffic within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 8 points while TRANSIT does not fall
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after PARKS jumps and TRANSIT is stable or higher.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling WORKPLACES and persistently low TRANSIT implies a renewed mobility restriction or compliance shock that suppresses discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 while TRANSIT stays below -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES falls below -20 and TRANSIT stays below -40.

mechanism_narrative: When residential stickiness remains above baseline but work and transit mobility stop deteriorating, consumers regain confidence to shop in person, producing a retail rebound with a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 and WORKPLACES stop falling
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days when RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 and WORKPLACES stop declining.
